name: Tenderlake
description:
Tenderlake gives Claude direct access to more than a decade of public procurement records: tenders, contract awards, frameworks, call-offs and forward plans from the United Kingdom, every EU member state and the wider EEA including Switzerland and Norway, with US and Canadian federal procurement as an add-on. Notices are translated into English with the original preserved, and organisation names are matched so one buyer reads as one buyer however it was written.

For Tenderlake Monitor users, the connector brings your workspace into the conversation: list your folders and the notices in them, read full notice details in English or the original language, and review your saved AI searches and demand signals.

For workgroups with Tenderlake Analyst, Claude can also research the buyers, competitors and markets you sell into. Ask what a named buyer has awarded, to whom and at what value, and what its planning notices signal. Ask what a competitor has won and from which buyers. Scan a market by meaning rather than keyword to see where demand is strongest and whether spend is consolidating. Find the route in: whether a buyer purchases through frameworks, dynamic purchasing systems or open competition, and who has called off through a given framework. Every answer cites the notices, dates, values and organisations behind it, so findings can be checked before a bid decision rests on them.

Users connect by signing in to Tenderlake and approving the connection; no API keys are handled. Results are limited to your workgroup's subscription regions. Analyst tools are metered in credits, with every call recorded in a ledger visible to the workgroup administrator. Tenderlake receives only the specific lookups Claude makes, never the conversation itself.

Requires a Tenderlake account on a paid subscription, with AI-assistant access granted by a workgroup administrator; not available on the free plan or free trial. Analyst research tools require the Tenderlake Analyst plan.

_published_faq.name: How do I add Tenderlake to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Tenderlake to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://mcp.tenderlake.com/mcp. This server requires OAuth, so complete the login prompt after you connect.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the Tenderlake MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tenderlake lists 24 MCP tools, including buyer_awards, buyer_frameworks, buyer_notices, create_organisation, framework_calloffs, get_ai_search_matches, get_mcp_status, get_notice_details, list_ai_searches, list_demand_signals, list_folder_notices, and list_folders.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to Tenderlake?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 18, 2026, alternatives to Tenderlake in productivity on the Manufact MCP catalog include Autodesk Product Help, BoardWise, FlagStat, Keenable Web Search, and PomoDial.
Tenderlake requires authentication. Connect it in Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor and complete the OAuth login prompt.
Tenderlake is developed by Tenderlake Ltd. It is listed as community on the Claude connector directory.
